newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on Lujiazui.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on Lujiazui.

text.p: Shanghai B shares reversed early losses on a rise of market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development on the news that it planned to make a four-for-10 bonus issue, brokers said.
Shanghai Lujiazui rose $0.018 or 2.25 percent to $0.818, on volume of 437,000 shares, after resuming trade this afternoon.
The index edged up 0.017 points or 0.04 percent to 46.810 points, on volume of 8.4 million shares worth $2.0 million. Of 41 B shares, 34 traded with 16 up, six flat and 12 down.
The A index soared nearly six percent in heavy trading, with funds from the Shenzhen market flowing in, brokers said.

"The exchange held a meeting on the Shanghai B share market last week and asked investors to keep confidence in the market, a sign that the government is concerned about recent falls in the B shares market," one broker said.
Officials were not immediately available for comment.
"After consolidation, the market will rally again as there is little room for further falls with the index so low," a second broker said.
"Today's surge of Shenzhen B shares will help support the Shanghai B share index in the coming days," he added. Shenzhen B share index rose by 5.51 percent, with turnover doubling.

Shanghai Rubber Belt was the star on speculative buying, jumping $0.016 or 13.33 percent to $0.136, on volume of 25,300 shares. Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere traded the most on institutional liquidation, down $0.008 or 2.06 percent to $0.380, on volume of 1.6 million shares.
Shanghai A share index jumped in active trade, encouraged by the recent strong performance of the Shenzhen market, brokers said.
They said that some major Shenzhen investors were seen stepping into the Shanghai bourse late in the session.

The A index soared 57.943 points or 5.79 percent to 1058.829 points, on volume of 783.7 million shares worth 7.2 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index jumped 125.490 points or 5.00 percent to 2633.063 points.
Shanghai Fello was the star on speculative buying, surging 1.70 yuan or 18.37 percent to 10.95 yuan, on volume of 23.3 million shares.
